title: Italy: CONAI membership and environmental contribution
summary: A business placing packaging on the Italian market generally joins the CONAI consortium and pays the environmental contribution (CAC) on the packaging it places, reporting through the material consortium for each packaging type.

sources.title: CONAI — Joining CONAI / Mandatory subjects and enrollment procedures
sources.note: MAJOR OPEN QUESTION, not resolved this pass -- flagging rather than guessing, same discipline as the PPWR AR row held at PR #4. CONAI's own English page states in as many words: 'Foreign companies are not obliged to join CONAI, but they may do so voluntarily.' It grounds the membership duty in Art. 221 of D.Lgs. 152/2006 ('producer and user companies are responsible ... and consequently required to join'), and the €15,500-46,500 fine for non-joining applies to 'producers of packaging' -- but the foreign-company carve-out is asserted on this page without its own citation. If accurate, this row may not apply to CFM's typical customer at all (a non-Italian-established seller shipping into Italy) -- responsibility may instead fall on whichever Italian-established party imports/distributes the goods, similar in shape to the Spanish RPP row's first-distributor fallback (es.epr.authorised-representative, same batch) or a customs importer-of-record. This needs the actual text of Art. 221 (and its definition of 'produttore' / 'importatore', likely Art. 218) read before either publishing this row as-is or rescoping it -- do not assume the current applies_when (no establishment condition) is correct just because it is the safe/broad direction; it could be actively wrong for the primary customer segment this tool serves.

sources.title: Guida all'adesione e all'applicazione del Contributo Ambientale CONAI (CNA Firenze, 2023)
sources.note: Independent secondary source corroborating the same foreign-company exemption verbatim: 'Non sono obbligate ad aderire al CONAI (ma ne hanno facoltà) le Imprese estere e le Imprese agricole' (foreign companies and agricultural businesses are not obliged to join CONAI, though they may do so voluntarily) -- same construction as agricultural businesses, whose exemption IS traceable to a specific statute (Art. 11(2), Law 154/2016). Two independent sources agreeing is reassuring but neither is the statute itself; the €200/€300 exemption thresholds this same guide describes are for the CAC environmental-contribution declaration, not registration, and are a separate, smaller question than the foreign-company one above.
